title: Goal reached: staged redemption
objectives: Distinguish a one-time goal from a regular-income goal, and the tool for each.
Explain why staged redemption beats a single redemption.
body_md:
When the goal arrives, the money has to leave the portfolio in the right shape.

## Two kinds of goal

- A one-time goal — an education fee, a house down payment, a wedding: redeem from the debt or liquid portion as payments fall due.
- A regular-income goal — retirement: set up a Systematic Withdrawal Plan, which redeems a fixed amount each month.

## Why staged, not one shot

- A single redemption on one day puts the whole amount at that day's price and tax treatment.
- Staged redemption matches the money to the payments, so nothing sits in equity that will be spent next month.
- The rest stays invested, so it keeps earning while it waits its turn.

## Before the first redemption

Check the exit load on recent instalments, refer the tax question to a CA, and confirm the nominee, bank account and KYC are current. Money moving out is the worst time to discover an outdated bank mandate.
example: A client's daughter starts college in July and the fees are due each term. The first term is redeemed from a liquid fund now; the rest stays in short-duration debt and is redeemed term by term.
say: We'll redeem as each payment falls due, so nothing sits in equity that you need next term.
Let's confirm your bank details and nominee before the first withdrawal.
never: Let's redeem it all today and park it in a savings account.
Withdrawals from your SIP are tax-free.

talk_track.title: Goal reached: staged redemption or SWP
talk_track.text: When the goal is reached and the client needs regular income, such as in retirement, we use a systematic withdrawal plan, which redeems a fixed amount every month. For a one-time goal, redeem from the safe portion as payments fall due, and keep the rest invested until its turn.

check.q: A one-time goal such as a college fee is best funded by…
o: Redeeming the whole corpus on day one
Redeeming from the debt or liquid portion as each payment falls due
An SWP for the next twenty years
check.why: A one-time goal is paid as payments fall due, from the safe portion, while the rest stays invested.

check.q: Which goal calls for an SWP?
o: A house down payment in 18 months
A regular-income goal such as retirement
check.why: An SWP redeems a fixed amount at regular intervals, which suits a monthly income need.

check.q: Why stage redemptions instead of making one?
o: Because the AMC limits redemptions to one a year
Because it matches the money to the payments and avoids one day's price and tax treatment
Because staged redemptions are always tax-free
Because exit loads rise with each redemption
check.why: Staged redemption matches cash to need and avoids putting the whole amount through one day's price and tax treatment.
